concerns.concern: Temperature independence of r0 does not rule out Joule heating. The favoured hot-spot (NEP) model is itself a diffusion model and should also give a temperature-dependent threshold through ρ_c(T), τ and D, yet both temperatures are fitted with one P_d.
concerns.quote: Joule heating caused by the leakage current can be excluded because the quenching does not depend on temperature.

concerns.concern: The critical temperature of the films is not stated. This matters because 5.6–5.8 K may be close to T_c, and the Outlook even speaks of reaching above it.
concerns.quote: The text also does not state T_c of the films used for D3.

concerns.concern: Identifying the µW-scale, micron-range suppression of Meissner screening with the nW-scale transport gate-controlled supercurrent effect is overstated. Calling it a 'genuine feature of superconductivity' implies the intrinsic field-effect picture the paper itself argues against.
concerns.quote: establishing the phenomenon as a genuine feature of superconductivity that is not restricted to transport.

concerns.concern: The claim of only weak correlation between r0 and gate voltage is not supported. Within each dataset r0 rises steeply with |V_G| because power and voltage are monotonically linked. The exclusion of a field effect rests only on onset-voltage drift between two clusters, which leaves a time-varying field effect (e.g., from trapped oxide charge) possible.
concerns.quote: Data of a plotted against gate voltage |VG| showing only weak correlation thereby ruling out a direct field effect.

concerns.concern: The 3D diffusion solution is used even though the favoured interpretation, quasiparticle diffusion in a 20 nm film, is effectively 2D. In 2D the profile is a K0 Bessel function, which changes the functional form of r0(P) and the inferred r_d and τ.
concerns.quote: The film is 20 nm thick and effectively 2D, where the steady-state solution is ρ ∝ K0(r/r_d)/(2πD d) rather than e^{-r/r_d}/r.

concerns.concern: The substrate-diffusion scenario is dismissed using the room-temperature thermal diffusivity of glass. At low temperature, and for quasi-ballistic non-equilibrium phonons that may reach the Si, the diffusivity can differ by orders of magnitude.
concerns.quote: 10⁻⁶ m²/s is the room-temperature thermal diffusivity of glass.

concerns.concern: The relevant thin-film screening length is the Pearl length (~3–6 µm), not λ, so the explanation of why the leads are unresolved is wrong. With this length comparable to the island size, the extraction of r0 depends strongly on the model, the assumed geometry and the temperature-dependent screening length.
concerns.quote: The gate and ohmic leads are barely resolved because their width is of order of the penetration depth (λ ∼ 240 nm, Table S2).

concerns.concern: No uncertainties are given for the fitted r_d and P_d, even though r0 is quoted with high precision and the two extraction methods assume different geometries.
concerns.quote: No uncertainties are given for the fitted r_d and P_d.

concerns.concern: The claim that suppression is reproducible at equal power for all devices contradicts the fitted P_d values, which differ by about 2.6× between devices. At 1 µW this gives r0 of about 0.59 µm versus 1.0 µm, and the device-to-device variation is not discussed.
concerns.quote: is reproducible given the same applied power P for all our devices.

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether r0 is measured from the gate apex or as the recession of the superconducting edge. The ~80 nm gate–island gap would bias the fitted parameters by about 15%.
concerns.quote: we assume that the quenching extends radially from the tip of the gate electrode up to a critical distance r0.

concerns.concern: The fitted relaxation time is compared to a hot-spot formation time and to a circuit-limited detector recovery time. Neither is the same quantity, so these comparisons lend unwarranted plausibility to τ≈0.7 ns.
concerns.quote: This is roughly ten times longer than the time for hot-spot formation reported in [13]
